scenes.headline: How a small language model writes a room as code
scenes.sub: SpatialLM: a point cloud in, walls, doors and boxes out
scenes.say: Hi, I'm Lintel! This model reads a scan of a room and writes the room back as code. Here's how.

scenes.text: Put a point-cloud encoder in front of an ordinary small language model, and train it to write every wall, door, window and box as one line of code.
scenes.say: The idea: an ordinary small language model, with a point cloud encoder in front, writes every wall, door, window and box as one line.

scenes.title: From a scan to point tokens

items.say: The cloud must stand upright, in metres, walls lined up.
Points snap to a grid two and a half centimetres wide.
The Sonata encoder halves it four times, to forty centimetre cells.
Each occupied cell is one token. Bigger rooms, longer prompts.

steps.say: The encoder gives one feature per occupied cell.
A small network stretches each to the language model's width.
They sit in the prompt like words, before the task and a code template.
The model writes one line per wall, door or box. Doors name their wall.

parts.say: Positions live in a fixed range, zero to thirty two metres.
Twelve hundred and eighty bins makes two and a half centimetres a step.

parts.note: every digit is its own token
parts.say: Integers only, and every digit costs a token.

steps.say: The paper's picture: encoder, projector, language model, prompt.
Out comes text, shown decoded to metres.
Drawn over the scan, it becomes walls and boxes.

scenes.title: Structured3D layout, F1 at 0.25
scenes.note: after pre-training on its own synthetic rooms
scenes.say: On a floor plan benchmark it beats both specialists, ninety four point three.

scenes.label: object F1 when trained on ScanNet alone
scenes.say: But only after pre-training. On the real scan set alone, two point nine.

scenes.text: The recipe is ordinary: encoder, projector, small language model. The thousands of designer rooms are what make it work.
scenes.say: The recipe is ordinary. The thousands of designer rooms make it work.

recap: One token per occupied 40 cm cell
Every wall and box is one line
Pre-training data does the heavy lifting
scenes.say: Points become cells, cells become tokens, tokens become a floor plan.
